mainTopic: Her כתובה and the יבם's inheritance based on her testimony, and which women may not testify that her husband died
overview: This amud opens at the end of a משנה about a woman who says her husband died. בית הלל argued that her word should not get her the money of her כתובה. בית שמאי answered from the wording of the כתובה, and בית הלל changed their minds. In the גמרא, רב חסדא adds that a יבם who married her based on her word also inherits his brother's property, learning this from the פסוק 'יקום על שם אחיו'. רב נחמן teaches that how she words her request in בית דין matters: if she asks to remarry, she is believed and collects. If she asks only for her כתובה, she is not believed at all. Mixed requests end in תיקו. A new משנה lists five women who may not testify that her husband died, because they may hate her. The גמרא asks about her father-in-law's daughter and compares this list with a list of seven, which follows רבי יהודה. Last, it asks about a future mother-in-law through יבום, and this question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית הלל: The brothers do not inherit based on her word
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל push back against בית שמאי's argument. They point out that the brothers do not inherit their dead brother's property based on the woman's testimony, so her word does not work for money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: [בית הלל said:] We see that the brothers do not take over the inheritance based on her word!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of בית הלל's reply in the משנה. They show that her testimony, which is accepted for remarrying, is not accepted for money, because the brothers cannot inherit based on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי had argued: if we trust her for the serious matter of marriage, we should surely trust her for the lighter matter of money. בית הלל knock this down with a case where her word clearly does not work for money: the brothers' inheritance. So permission to remarry does not automatically bring money rights with it.

keyTerms.meaning: brothers (here, the dead husband's brothers, who would be his heirs)
based on her word, her testimony

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument that started earlier in the משנה. The 'her' is the woman who reported that her husband died, and בית הלל are the ones speaking.

phrases.english: that the brothers do not come into
the inheritance based on her word!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין הָאַחִין נִכְנָסִין לַנַּחֲלָה עַל פִּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's earlier קל וחומר from the משנה, which comes before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that trust for remarrying automatically includes trust for money.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a clear case, the brothers' inheritance, where her word works for marriage but not for money.

steps.title: בית שמאי: Learn it from the wording of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the כתובה document itself connects her money to her ability to remarry. It says, 'If you marry another man, take what is written for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: But we can learn it from the כתובה document! The husband writes for her: 'If you marry another man, you will take what is written for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי answer בית הלל's objection by pointing to the actual words written in every כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה ties her collecting the money to her being free to marry someone else. Since we already allow her to remarry based on her word, the condition in the document is met, so she collects. The brothers' inheritance has no such link to her remarrying, so it is a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: the כתובה document, the marriage contract
but surely, isn't it so that

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a way of learning law from the exact wording of a common document. רב חסדא will build on this idea in the גמרא.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
But we can learn from the marriage contract document,
for he writes for her:
that if you marry another man,
you will take what is written for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: וַהֲלֹא מִסֵּפֶר כְּתוּבָּה נִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's objection from the brothers' inheritance.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases using the wording of the כתובה, which makes her money depend on her right to remarry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her word never works for money, just as with the brothers' inheritance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה links her money to her remarriage, so once she may remarry, she collects.

steps.title: בית הלל change their ruling
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל accept the argument and start ruling like בית שמאי: she collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל changed their minds and ruled like בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by telling us that בית הלל were convinced and switched to בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The final law is that a woman trusted to remarry based on her own word also collects her כתובה. This is one of the rare cases where בית הלל retract and agree with בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: and they went back on their view, retracted
to rule, to teach the law

steps.whatToRemember: Final law of the משנה: she remarries AND collects her כתובה based on her own testimony, because the כתובה links the money to her remarriage.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel retracted
to rule in accordance with the words of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל accept בית שמאי's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She collects her כתובה based on her own testimony.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The יבם inherits based on her word
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if the woman did יבום based on her own testimony, her יבם takes over his dead brother's property based on that testimony too.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. רב חסדא said: If she married the יבם, her יבם takes over the inheritance based on her word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רב חסדא adding a new rule. In the case of יבום, the יבם does inherit based on her word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the brothers do NOT inherit based on her word. רב חסדא says that once one brother actually married her as a יבם, that brother does inherit. This is a special result for the יבם only. It does not cancel the general rule about the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: she married the יבם, she did יבום
her יבם, the brother-in-law who marries her

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the משנה. The משנה is about the brothers in general. רב חסדא is about the one brother who actually did יבום with her.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Chisda said:
If she entered into levirate marriage,
her yavam comes into the inheritance based on her word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה, limiting בית הלל's point about the brothers in the case of an actual יבם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבם who married her based on her testimony inherits his brother's property based on that same testimony.

steps.title: If they learned from a כתובה, we can learn from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא argues that if בית שמאי could learn law from the words of a כתובה, we can surely learn from the words of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learned from the wording of a כתובה. Shall we not learn from the wording of the תורה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא sets up his proof. He points to בית שמאי's method and says the same method works even better with a פסוק. The next step brings the actual פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי tied her money to her remarriage because of the words of the כתובה. רב חסדא says the תורה's words carry at least as much weight. If the תורה ties the יבם's inheritance to his marrying her, the inheritance should follow the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: learning from the wording of the כתובה
learning from the wording of the תורה

phrases.english: They interpreted the wording of a marriage contract,
phrases.notes: 'They' are בית שמאי, from the משנה.

phrases.english: shall we not interpret the wording of the Torah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵם דָּרְשׁוּ מִדְרַשׁ כְּתוּבָּה אָנוּ לֹא נִדְרוֹשׁ מִדְרַשׁ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב חסדא's ruling, using בית שמאי's method as a model.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that the יבם inherits based on her word.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית שמאי's accepted method of learning from the wording of the כתובה, applied with even more force to the תורה.

steps.title: The פסוק: He shall succeed in his brother's name
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings the פסוק 'He shall succeed in the name of his brother.' Since the יבם has in fact taken his brother's place by marrying her, he inherits too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה says, 'He shall succeed in the name of his brother,' and he did succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the פסוק that his proof rests on and applies it to our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is understood as giving the יבם his brother's inheritance once he takes his brother's place through יבום. Here the יבום really happened, based on her trusted word. So the inheritance follows automatically, just as the כתובה money followed her remarriage.

keyTerms.meaning: he shall succeed in the name of his brother (דברים 25:6)
the Merciful One, a name for God when quoting the תורה
and he did succeed, he did take the place

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: inheritance follows the יבום. Once the יבם married her based on her testimony, he has taken his brother's place, so he inherits based on that testimony too.

phrases.english: "He shall succeed in the name of his brother"
the Merciful One said,
and here he did succeed.
phrases.notes: He married her, so he took his brother's place, and the inheritance comes with that.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא וַהֲרֵי קָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual פסוק that the previous step promised.
steps.raayaObject: The יבם inherits based on her word.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 25:6, 'יקום על שם אחיו,' which ties the inheritance to the יבום that took place.

steps.title: What she asks for decides whether she is believed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן: if she says 'my husband died, permit me to marry,' she may marry and collects her כתובה. If she says 'give me my כתובה,' she may not even marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: If a woman comes to בית דין and says, 'My husband died, permit me to marry,' they permit her to marry and give her her כתובה. If she says, 'Give me my כתובה,' they do not even permit her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new rule. How the woman words her request decides whether בית דין believes her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her goal is to remarry, we trust her, and the money follows along with that. If her goal is the money, her whole testimony becomes suspect, so she loses the right to remarry as well.
steps.confusionAlert: She does not just lose the money. When she asks only for the כתובה, she is not allowed to remarry either.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
If she came to the court
and said: "My husband died,
permit me to marry"
they permit her to marry
and they give her her marriage contract.
If she said: "Give me my marriage contract,"
they do not even permit her to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of her collecting the כתובה on her own word, and adds a limit based on her motive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking to remarry: she is believed and also collects the כתובה. Asking only for the כתובה: she is not believed at all.

steps.title: Why asking for money ruins her testimony
steps.stepSummary: The reason: she came with the כתובה money in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? She came with the כתובה in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's second ruling and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her request shows that money is her main goal. Someone after money might lie, so we no longer trust her claim that the husband died.

keyTerms.meaning: She came with the כתובה in mind

phrases.english: What is the reason?
She came with the marriage contract in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of רב נחמן's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why she loses even the right to remarry
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her request shows her motive is money, so her testimony is suspect.

steps.title: She asks to remarry first, then for the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: What if she says 'permit me to marry and give me my כתובה'? Does mentioning money show a money motive, or do people simply list everything they are owed?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If she says 'Permit me to marry and give me my כתובה,' what is the law? Since she mentioned her כתובה, maybe she came for the money. Or perhaps a person tells the court everything he has coming to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about a mixed case: she asks for both, with remarriage first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says any mention of money reveals a money motive. The other side says it is normal to list all your claims in court, so mentioning the money proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
"Permit me to marry
and give me my marriage contract" — what is the law?
Since she mentioned her marriage contract,
she came with the marriage contract in mind,
or perhaps:
every matter that a person has coming to him
he tells to the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב נחמן's rule on a case where she makes both requests.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does mentioning the כתובה after asking to remarry show a money motive?

steps.title: She asks for the כתובה first, then to remarry
steps.stepSummary: Even if listing all claims is normal, what if she mentions the כתובה first? Maybe that clearly shows a money motive, or maybe she thinks the money is part of being freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a person tells the court everything he has coming to him, what if she says 'Give me my כתובה and permit me to marry'? Here she certainly came for the money. Or perhaps not, since she does not know what makes her permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first one. It switches the order so that the money comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting money first looks more strongly like a money motive. On the other hand, she may simply not understand the process and think that collecting the כתובה is part of what frees her to remarry.

phrases.english: [And if you say
every matter that a person has coming to him
he tells to the court]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. They pick up the second side of the first question.

phrases.english: "Give me my marriage contract
and permit me to marry" — what is the law?
Here certainly
she came with the marriage contract in mind,
or perhaps:
since she does not know by what she becomes permitted?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the lenient side of step 9 and asks about the reversed order.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does putting the כתובה first show a money motive, or just confusion about the process?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: תיקו: the question stands without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof is found for either side. The case where she asks for the כתובה first stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Asking to remarry means she is believed. Asking only for money means she is not believed. Asking for both, especially with the money first, is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions from steps 9 and 10.

steps.title: Five women who cannot testify that her husband died
steps.stepSummary: Everyone is believed to testify that her husband died, except her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her יבמה, and her husband's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone is believed to testify for her, except her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her יבמה, and her husband's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five women whose testimony that the husband died is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally even one witness, including a woman, is enough to free her. These five women stand in a family relationship with her that the משנה treats as untrustworthy for this testimony. The גמרא will discuss them further.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
All are believed to testify for her,
except her mother-in-law and her mother-in-law's daughter,
and her co-wife, and her yevama,
phrases.notes: Her yevama is the wife of her husband's brother, the woman who would share the יבם with her.

phrases.english: and her husband's daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about who may testify that her husband died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is believed to testify that the husband died, except these five women.

steps.title: Why a divorce document is different from death testimony
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the suspected women can bring a גט because the written document itself proves the facts, unlike testimony about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a גט and death? A גט is a written document that proves itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its list of suspected women. It explains why these same women may still deliver a גט, even though they cannot testify that the husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With death, everything rests on the woman's word, so a woman who might want to hurt her could lie. With a גט, the document itself is the evidence. Her word is not doing the work, so her possible hatred does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Death (here, testimony that the husband died)
The writing proves (the document speaks for itself)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basic principle of the section: these women are disqualified only where we must rely on their word alone.

phrases.english: What is the difference between a bill of divorce and death?
That the writing proves it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the limits of the disqualification listed in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspected women may bring a גט, because the document proves itself. They are not believed about death, where only their word counts.

steps.title: Is the father-in-law's daughter also suspected?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about בת חמיה. It first suggests she might be believed, because בת חמותה's hatred comes from her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law for her father-in-law's daughter? Maybe the reason her mother-in-law's daughter is suspected is that her mother hates the daughter-in-law, so she hates her too. Here there is no such mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a woman not on the משנה's list. It lays out the first side: she might be believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בת חמיה is the husband's sister from his father's other wife. If בת חמותה is suspected only because she takes on her mother's hatred, then בת חמיה has no such mother and should be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the scholars
Her father-in-law's daughter (from a different wife)

phrases.english: Gemara: A dilemma was raised before them:
The daughter of her father-in-law, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means a daughter of the father-in-law from another wife, not the mother-in-law's daughter.

phrases.english: The reason for the mother-in-law's daughter
is because there is a mother who hates her,
so she also hates her,
but here there is no mother who hates her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the list from step 12 also covers a relative it does not mention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is בת חמיה disqualified like בת חמותה? It depends on the reason for בת חמותה's hatred.

steps.title: The other side: resentment over the family's food
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe בת חמותה hates her because the daughter-in-law eats the family's food. Then בת חמיה feels the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the mother-in-law's daughter hates her because she says, 'She is eating my mother's food.' Then the father-in-law's daughter would also say, 'She is eating my family's food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question. Here the father-in-law's daughter would be suspected too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hatred comes from jealousy over the household's resources, the mother has nothing to do with it. Any daughter of that household would resent her, so בת חמיה would also be disqualified.

phrases.english: Or perhaps the reason for the mother-in-law's daughter
is that she says: 'She is eating my mother's food,'
here too she says:
'She eats the food of my father's house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two sides of the question begun in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the hatred about the food, which would include בת חמיה, or about the mother, which would not?

steps.title: Proof from the count of five women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that says 'five women' that בת חמיה is believed. Otherwise the list would have six.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: everyone is believed to testify for her except five women. If the father-in-law's daughter were also suspected, there would be six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to settle the question. It reasons from the exact number given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says exactly five. Adding בת חמיה would make six, so the count suggests she is not disqualified and is believed.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
All are believed to testify for her
except for five women.
phrases.notes: These are the five from step 12: mother-in-law, her daughter, co-wife, יבמה, and husband's daughter.

phrases.english: And if it were so, there would be six!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַכֹּל נֶאֱמָנִין לְהַעִידָהּ חוּץ מֵחָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from steps 14 and 15.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's exact count of five disqualified women.

steps.title: Both daughters may count as one category
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: if the reason is the family's food, both daughters fall under one heading, so the count stays five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the mother-in-law's daughter is suspected because she says, 'She eats my family's food.' Then there is no difference between the mother-in-law's daughter and the father-in-law's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the number five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hatred is about the food, בת חמותה and בת חמיה share one reason. The ברייתא counts them as a single category, so the list can include בת חמיה and still say 'five.' The proof falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about בת חמיה depends on why בת חמותה is suspected. The count of 'five' does not decide it, because both daughters may be one category.

phrases.english: Perhaps the reason for the mother-in-law's daughter
is that she says: 'She is eating the food of my father's house,'
so there is no difference whether it is the mother-in-law's daughter
or the father-in-law's daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 16 by using the second side from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the number five. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The count could treat both daughters as one category, so 'five' proves nothing.

steps.title: A source that lists seven women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count of five with a source that says seven women are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: except for seven women!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that says seven women are not believed, not five. That suggests extra women, maybe בת חמיה, are counted on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 kept the count at five by putting both daughters under one heading. A list of seven shows that some source does count more women separately, so the count of five seems shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
Except for seven women!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of five that step 17 defended
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 17's claim that בת חמותה and בת חמיה are counted together as one category
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source lists seven, which suggests that בת חמיה is listed as her own category and is not folded into בת חמותה

steps.title: The seven-women list follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The list of seven is רבי יהודה's view. He adds אשת אב and כלה to the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: That source is רבי יהודה. As we learned: רבי יהודה also adds a father's wife and a daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the list of seven belongs to רבי יהודה, who adds two women to the regular five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two extra women are not בת חמיה. They are the stepmother (אשת אב) and the daughter-in-law (כלה). So the seven does not prove that בת חמיה is a separate category.

phrases.english: That one is Rabbi Yehuda.
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda adds
also a father's wife and the daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the seven-women list
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven shows that בת חמיה is counted on her own
steps.terutzMaskana: The seven is רבי יהודה's list, and his additions are אשת אב and כלה

steps.title: The חכמים say the two are already included
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that אשת אב is covered by בת הבעל and כלה is covered by חמותה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: a father's wife is included in the husband's daughter, and a daughter-in-law is included in her mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה. They say his two additions are already part of the five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their idea is that hatred goes both ways. If the husband's daughter hates the stepmother, the stepmother hates her back. If the mother-in-law hates the daughter-in-law, the daughter-in-law hates her back. So each pair is one category.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אָב הֲרֵי הִיא בִּכְלַל בַּת הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: A father's wife is included in the husband's daughter,
a daughter-in-law is included in her mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים respond to רבי יהודה's addition
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's adding of אשת אב and כלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hatred is mutual, so each added woman already falls under her partner's heading

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the hatred is not mutual
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the food reason only works one way, so the pairs cannot be lumped together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה would say: it makes sense that the mother-in-law hates the daughter-in-law, since she says 'she eats my food.' But why would the daughter-in-law hate the mother-in-law? It makes sense that the husband's daughter hates the father's wife, since she says 'she eats my mother's food.' But why would the father's wife hate the husband's daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reply to the חכמים. The reason one woman hates the other does not apply in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother-in-law and the husband's daughter resent the other woman for eating 'their' food. The daughter-in-law and the stepmother are the ones eating, so they have no such complaint. Hatred in one direction therefore does not prove hatred in the other.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda [would say]:
It makes sense that her mother-in-law hates the daughter-in-law,
since she says: She is eating my food.
But the daughter-in-law, what is the reason
that she hates her mother-in-law?
It makes sense regarding the husband's daughter
that she hates the father's wife,
since she says: She is eating my mother's food.
But the father's wife, what is the reason
that she hates the husband's daughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה defends himself against the חכמים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the reason for hatred is one-directional
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hatred is mutual, so each pair is one category
steps.terutzMaskana: The food reason only works one way, so the pairs are not automatically one category

steps.title: Then why does רבי יהודה add them at all?
steps.stepSummary: If these two women have no reason to hate, why does רבי יהודה add them to the list?
steps.simpleTranslation: So why does he add two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the stepmother and daughter-in-law have no reason to hate, they should not be on the list at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step showed that these two women do not share the food reason. But רבי יהודה does add them, so he must think they are suspect. He needs his own reason for their hatred.

keyTerms.meaning: So what then? (pushes back on the last answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not against the חכמים. It asks how רבי יהודה's own answer fits with his adding these two women.

phrases.english: So why does he add two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the daughter-in-law and stepmother have no reason to hate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they have no reason to hate, there is no basis for adding them

steps.title: A different reason: she reports everything
steps.stepSummary: The daughter-in-law and stepmother hate the other woman because she reports everything they do to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: why does the daughter-in-law hate her mother-in-law? Because she reveals to her son everything she does. The father's wife also hates the husband's daughter, because she reveals to her father everything she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason רבי יהודה adds these two women. Each one hates the other woman for telling on her to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two women do hate the other woman, but for a different reason than the food complaint. Because the reason is different, רבי יהודה counts them as separate categories, which brings the list to seven.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה counts seven women because the daughter-in-law and stepmother hate for their own reason (being reported on). The חכמים count five because they see each pair as one category.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source that lists seven women. It is רבי יהודה's view, and it does not prove that בת חמיה is counted on her own.

phrases.english: Rather: the daughter-in-law, what is the reason
that she hates her mother-in-law?
Because she reveals to her son everything she does,

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אָב נָמֵי סָנְיָא לְבַת הַבַּעַל —
phrases.english: a father's wife also hates the husband's daughter,
because she reveals to her father everything she does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כַּלָּה מַאי טַעְמָא סָנְיָא לַחֲמוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a new, separate reason for the hatred
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughter-in-law and stepmother have no reason to hate, so why are they listed?
steps.terutzMaskana: They hate because the other woman reports everything to the husband, so they are separate categories

steps.title: The חכמים: hatred always comes back
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use a פסוק to show that when one person hates another, the hatred becomes mutual. So the pairs can be lumped together after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? They hold: "As in water face answers to face, so is the heart of a person to a person."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with רבי יהודה's argument that the food reason only works one way. They answer with a פסוק showing that hatred is always returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said each woman needs her own reason to hate. The חכמים say no separate reason is needed: if the mother-in-law hates the daughter-in-law, the daughter-in-law will hate her back. So חמותה already covers כלה, and בת הבעל already covers אשת אב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the חכמים who argue with רבי יהודה
Like water reflecting face to face
A person's heart toward another person, meaning feelings are returned

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
"As in water, face answers to face,"
so is the heart of a person to a person."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the חכמים' view against רבי יהודה's reasoning from steps 21 and 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that each woman in a pair needs her own separate reason to hate.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק showing that hatred is naturally returned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the food reason works only one way, the two sides of each pair might seem to need separate listing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hatred is mutual, so one reason covers both sides, and the list stays at five.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: that פסוק is about תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the proof. The פסוק is talking about learning תורה, not about hatred between people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He says: that פסוק is written about דברי תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה does not accept the חכמים' פסוק. He answers that the פסוק has a different subject: learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is not about feelings between people, it proves nothing about mutual hatred. So רבי יהודה still says each woman needs her own reason to hate. That is why he lists seven women, not five.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to one question: is hatred automatically mutual? The חכמים say yes, so five women are listed. רבי יהודה says no, so seven are listed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
That verse is written about words of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָהִיא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the פסוק brought by the חכמים in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק as proof that hatred between people is mutual.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about Torah learning, not human feelings.

steps.title: What about a mother-in-law who comes later?
steps.stepSummary: A question from ארץ ישראל: can a woman who may become this widow's mother-in-law in the future, through יבום, testify about her?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר עויא said: In ארץ ישראל they asked: what is the law for a mother-in-law who comes later? Does she think ahead that the husband will die, the widow will fall to the יבם (her son), and so she hates her already? Or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the list. It asks whether the brother-in-law's mother, who is not yet her mother-in-law, is also suspected of hating her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real mother-in-law hates her daughter-in-law because the daughter-in-law will eat from the family's money. Here the woman would only become her mother-in-law if the husband dies and the widow marries her son through יבום. The question is whether a woman plans so far ahead that she already hates her now.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked in the West, meaning in ארץ ישראל
A mother-in-law who comes later, through יבום
Does it enter her mind? Does she think that far ahead?
The dead husband's brother, who may do יבום

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the husband's own mother, who is already on the list. It is the mother of the brother-in-law, who would only become her mother-in-law later through יבום.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Avya said:
They asked in the West:
phrases.notes: "The West" is how people in בבל referred to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Her mother-in-law who comes afterward, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the brother-in-law's mother. She becomes her mother-in-law only if the widow marries her son through יבום.

phrases.english: Does it enter her mind
that the husband will die
and she will fall before the yavam
and so she hates her, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר עַוְיָא בָּעוּ בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה and חכמים debate and opens a new question about who counts as a mother-in-law on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a possible future mother-in-law, through יבום, already suspected of hating the woman, so that she cannot testify?
